title: `-0.0` and `0.0`
description: DuckDB keeps `-0.0` through `ORDER BY` and sorts it as a peer of `0.0`: both zeros get the same sort key, so the next key or the input order decides. `1.0 / -0.0 = -inf` natively. (Corrected 2026-11-04: this said `-0.0` sorts before `0.0`; the cited test sorts by `v, id`, so `id` broke the tie.)
Shim: sverify's SQL normalizes `-0.0` to `0.0` on every read and after every operation that can make it (`Dialect.canon`).

Round 4 (probes): `ORDER BY v` alone keeps the zeros in their input order, both signs kept: -0.0, 0.0, -0.0 and 0.0, -0.0, 0.0 come out as they went in, ascending and descending, for DOUBLE and FLOAT. So they are peers.
The docs are silent on how `ORDER BY` treats `-0.0`, NaN and ties: a docs gap. No upstream test pins that the two zeros are peers; it may change between versions.
reference: Substrait: `fp64` is IEEE. The spec says nothing about grouping or ordering `-0.0`.
Lean: one zero (#89), so `1.0 / -0.0` is `inf`, not IEEE's `-inf`. Decided on #209: one zero, so no Lean change.

evidence.sql: SELECT v, 1.0 / v FROM zero_probe ORDER BY v, id;

evidence.note: EncodeFloat/EncodeDouble give -0.0 and 0.0 the same key
FLOAT/DOUBLE columns carried separately to keep their sign
orders by v, id with -0.0 at id 1: the tie is broken by id

provenance.notes: Contradicts the earlier reading that -0.0 sorts first; the description is corrected. A probe of ORDER BY v alone, with -0.0 after 0.0 in the input, is on the probe round's list.

provenance.checked_by: characterization pipeline round 4 (probes; duckdb 2.0.0, Python, macOS arm64)
provenance.notes: `python -m sverify_dev.probe --observations --write` runs each query on a fresh connection under `TimeZone = 'UTC'` (or its own setup) and records the rows or the error as they come; `tests/test_probe.py::test_observations_are_current` checks they are current. Confirms round 2's correction: `ORDER BY v` alone leaves the zeros in their input order.

evidence.note: silent on -0.0, NaN and the order of ties
signbit kept through ORDER BY v, id; the peer order of the zeros is not pinned
